title: Quantum-kernel SVM (exact classical statevector simulation) versus an RBF control on identical q=8 PCA features
declaration: Written and committed before any E9 evaluation. At the commit that adds this file none of results/E9_primary.json, results/E9_folds.csv, results/E9_tuning.json or results/E9_diagnostics.json exists. Any later change is appended to amendments, never edited in place.

code.note: git_head is the commit that contains the pinned code; at finalization git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no printed nothing. The exact code is pinned by the SHA-256 values below; the runner re-verifies them and refuses to run on a mismatch.

folds.note: the same 15 outer and 45 inner splits are used for the QSVM and for every control; no fold is re-drawn

conditions.features: src.common.feature on the reconstruction; byte-identical arrays to E4

preprocessing.pca: src.pca.PCA(n_components=8) fitted on the training fold only; the same Z is given to the QSVM and to the RBF control
preprocessing.quantum_scaler: AngleScaler fitted on the same training fold: u=(z-min)/(max-min) with training min/max, constant component -> u=0.5, theta=s*pi*u, test values never clipped

quantum_model.simulator: exact statevector, numpy complex128; no shots, no noise in the primary run
quantum_model.feature_map: zz (IQP): D(theta)=exp(i[sum_i theta_i Z_i + sum_{i<j}(pi-theta_i)(pi-theta_j) Z_i Z_j]), U(theta)=[D(theta) H^otimes q]^L
quantum_model.kernel: K(x,x') = |<phi(x)|phi(x')>|^2; unit diagonal, PSD by construction

primary_family.contrast: QSVM minus RBF control, paired within fold
primary_family.multiplicity: Holm-Bonferroni over the 4 primary p-values, family-wise alpha = 0.05
primary_family.significance_rule: a test is called significant only if the Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 AND the patient-clustered bootstrap 95% CI of the paired difference excludes 0; if exactly one gate passes the test is called inconclusive; otherwise not significant
primary_family.no_alternative_rule: no metric, subset, level, q or L outside this list may be promoted to a primary claim after seeing results

budget.statement: 4 C x 4 s = 16 for the QSVM and 4 C x 4 g = 16 for the RBF(q=8) control, so the two tuning budgets match. The control grid extends the frozen E4 grid [0.1, 1, 10] by one decade at the low end because 186 of 390 E4 selections landed on the 0.1 edge; this is stated here, before E9.

grids.selection_protocol: mean balanced accuracy over the 3 inner StratifiedGroupKFold folds of the outer training set; PCA and AngleScaler refitted inside every inner training fold
grids.tie_break: first in the declared grid order, i.e. smallest C, then smallest s (respectively g)

grid_edge_rule.trigger: after the base grid, if the selected value of a parameter is the minimum or maximum of its current grid
grid_edge_rule.step: append one value beyond that edge: x10 for C and g, x2 for s
grid_edge_rule.evaluation: re-evaluate the full Cartesian product of the extended grid
grid_edge_rule.cap: at most one extension per parameter and at most two per fold; worst case 6x6 = 36 configs
grid_edge_rule.symmetry: the rule is applied identically to the QSVM and to the RBF control; differing extension counts are recorded and reported, and are never a reason to re-tune after seeing outer-fold results
grid_edge_rule.precedent: same keys and cap as config.EDGE_MAX_EXTENSIONS = 2 used for M1/M2 in results/hyperparams.json

fold_test.variance: (1/J + n_test/n_train) * s_d^2, s_d the sample SD (ddof=1) of the 15 paired fold differences

bootstrap.cluster: patient (soft confusion counts summed per patient)
bootstrap.seeds: numpy SeedSequence([2026, 41, test_id]), integer keys only

also_report_bonferroni.note: the per-test Bonferroni level, a conservative companion to the Holm-adjusted test; reported alongside the alpha=0.05 MDE for every test

mde.interpretation: post hoc sensitivity description computed from the observed s_d of each test; it does not enter the decision rule and is not a prospective power calculation

failure_handling.rule: every fold x level x model produces a row; nothing is dropped
failure_handling.solver_non_optimal: SVM_QP status, iterations and KKT gap are recorded; if the solve raises or returns no x, alpha and the metric are NaN, the row keeps status='failed', and the count n_failed is reported next to every affected test
failure_handling.non_psd: K is PSD by construction; psd_report(K).min_eig is recorded. If min_eig < -1e-10 the run is flagged non_psd=true in E9_diagnostics.json and reported; the primary analysis is unchanged and no eigenvalue clipping is applied
failure_handling.nan_metric: kept in results/E9_folds.csv; the paired test uses finite pairs only and reports J_used; if J_used < 15 this is stated with the p-value
failure_handling.single_class_fold: cannot occur by construction (StratifiedGroupKFold on both classes); if it does, recorded as status='single_class'

not_claimed: no quantum speedup: the simulator costs O(n^2 2^q) time and O(2^q) memory per state
no quantum hardware, no noise model beyond the explicit depolarizing diagnostic
a kernel computed on a simulator is a classical baseline, not evidence of quantum advantage

outputs.cache: data/cache/<sha256>.npy via src.cache.get_or_compute, key = SHA-256 of canonical JSON {key, config_hash}

exploratory.status: exploratory: excluded from the decision rule and from the Holm family. Reported with descriptive patient-clustered 95% bootstrap CIs only (B=10000, seed_keys=(42, run_id)); no p-values and no significance claims of any kind. Nothing here can be promoted to a primary claim after seeing results.
exploratory.budget_note: This list is fixed before execution; no run outside it is performed under the E9 name.
exploratory.hyperparameter_policy: Every run that changes the features or the kernel re-tunes (C, s) - or (C, g) for its paired RBF control - over the same pre-declared 4x4 grid and the same edge rule, on the inner folds of the same 15 outer splits. X7, X8 and X10 are the only runs that reuse primary hyperparameters, as stated in each entry.

runs.name: q sweep
runs.hyperparameters: re-tuned (C, s) on the inner folds of each of the 15 outer splits, 16-config grid, same edge rule
runs.paired_control: RBF on the same q PCA features, re-tuned (C, g) over the same 4x4 grid on the same folds
runs.reason: kernel-dimension ablation with a matched classical counterpart in every cell

runs.name: L sweep
runs.hyperparameters: re-tuned (C, s), 16-config grid, same edge rule
runs.paired_control: RBF on q=8 features, re-tuned (C, g); identical to the primary control because the features are unchanged

excluded.reason: L=3 was never in the plan (the plan was L in {1,2}); adding it now would be a post hoc degree of freedom

runs.name: product-state kernel (entanglement ablation)
runs.hyperparameters: re-tuned (C, s) over the same 16-config grid and edge rule; the product map is not given the ZZ-tuned s
runs.paired_control: RBF on q=8 features, re-tuned (C, g) over the same 4x4 grid on the same folds
runs.reason: removes the entangling ZZ phase; a fair ablation needs its own bandwidth, otherwise a gap could be a mistuned s

runs.name: linear SVM control
runs.map: none (linear kernel on the same 8 PCA features)
runs.hyperparameters: C tuned over the same 4-value grid on the same inner folds; no s

runs.name: R=8
runs.hyperparameters: re-tuned (C, s) on this cell's inner folds, 16-config budget, same edge rule
runs.paired_control: RBF on the same q=8 features at R=8, re-tuned (C, g) over the same 4x4 grid

runs.name: noise-free
runs.hyperparameters: re-tuned (C, s) on this cell's inner folds, 16-config budget, same edge rule
runs.paired_control: RBF on the same q=8 features, noise-free, re-tuned (C, g) over the same 4x4 grid

runs.name: Protocol B
runs.hyperparameters: the Protocol A model of the ORIGINAL level for that outer fold is reused unchanged
runs.protocol_b_definition: train on the original level only: PCA basis and AngleScaler are fitted on the original training features; each level's test features are projected with that original PCA basis and mapped with that original scaler
runs.no_clipping: test angles may leave [0, s*pi] because the original training range does not cover a reconstruction level; no clipping is applied, by design
runs.paired_control: RBF(q=8) fitted on the original features with the original PCA basis, applied to each level

runs.name: shot noise
runs.noise_application: binomial sampling is applied independently to the training Gram K_tr (symmetric, unit diagonal restored) and to the test-train cross Gram K_te,tr (no symmetry constraint); both are perturbed before the SVM sees them
runs.seeds: SeedSequence([2026, 81, run_id, outer_fold_index, draw_id]) with integer keys
runs.variant_note: raw keeps the unit diagonal and may be slightly indefinite; psd_project clips negative eigenvalues and does not renormalise the diagonal. psd_project is applied to the training Gram only: the test-train cross Gram has no PSD projection, so the projected variant is a pragmatic repair rather than a kernel induced by a feature map, and is labelled as such. The diagonal deviation after projection is reported.
runs.solvers: SVM_QP and SVM_SMO are both attempted on every noisy Gram; each row records its status, and a failed QP is reported as failed rather than silently replaced by SMO
runs.diagnostics: kernel-target alignment and min eigenvalue per level, S, draw and variant

runs.name: E4 RBF on the full PCA subspace
runs.reason: context for the q=8 compression, not a new comparison

runs.name: descriptive kernel diagnostics
quantities: kernel spectrum (all eigenvalues, min and max)
balanced accuracy at the re-tuned (C, s)
runs.reuse: q = 4 and q = 6 reuse the X1 runs; no duplicate fits
runs.reported_as: spectrum and rank table plus a KTA-versus-balanced-accuracy scatter across q and level
runs.note: descriptive only; no p-values, no significance claims, no decision rule

exploratory.reporting: one appendix table plus the multi-panel figure; never merged into the primary family

withdrawn.name: depolarizing fits
withdrawn.reason: superseded by Proposition 1: the depolarizing channel is a uniform rescaling of C on the y^T alpha = 0 subspace, so no fits are needed and none are run

propositions.name: depolarizing invariance
propositions.statement: For K_p = (1-p)K + (p/2^q) 1 1^T and any C > 0, the SVM trained on K_p with box C and the SVM trained on K with box (1-p)C have the same decision function.
proof: On y^T alpha = 0, alpha^T[(y y^T) o (1 1^T)] alpha = (y^T alpha)^2 = 0, so the K_p dual is D_p(alpha) = 1^T alpha - (1-p)/2 * alpha^T Q alpha with Q = (y y^T) o K.

alpha = beta/(1-p) maps the box 0 <= alpha <= C onto 0 <= beta <= (1-p)C and gives D_p(beta/(1-p)) = (1/(1-p)) [1^T beta - 1/2 beta^T Q beta], so both duals have the same maximizer up to this scaling.
Then f(x) = sum_i alpha_i y_i K_p(x,x_i) + b = sum_i beta_i y_i K(x,x_i) + b, because the constant (p/2^q) 1 1^T term is annihilated by y^T beta = 0 and the bias is unchanged by the KKT conditions.
propositions.implementation_caveat: SVM_QP adds config.SVM_RIDGE * I to the dual quadratic form, which breaks the invariance by O(ridge); T7 sets SVM_RIDGE = 0 to test the mathematical statement. Class-balanced C_i scale uniformly, so the statement holds with C_i -> (1-p) C_i.
propositions.consequence: the p in {0.01, 0.05} depolarizing runs are exactly the primary fits with C scaled by 1-p
